MARKET.head: Unified Wine & Grape Symposium returns to Sacramento in January 2027 with new sessions
MARKET.summ: The wine industry has had a tough year, both here in the U.S. and around the world. There has been a steady stream of bad news from all corners of the wine world and precious little good news to balance the scales.
takeaways: The Unified Wine & Grape Symposium, America's largest wine industry gathering, meets in Sacramento from January 26 to 28, 2027.
A new Tuesday general session, From Shelf to Vineyard, traces a $35 Napa Cabernet and a $12.99 Sauvignon Blanc back through the supply chain.

MARKET.head: Yarra Valley's Levantine Hill makes US debut at New York benefit dinner
MARKET.summ: Levantine Hill is expanding into the US, marking a “major milestone” for the family-owned Yarra Valley estate. Ranked number two in The Real Review’s Top Wineries of Australia 2026, the winery made its USA debut as the official wine partner of the American Australian Association’s 2026 New York Benefit Dinner.
takeaways: Levantine Hill, a family-owned Yarra Valley estate, became official wine partner of the American Australian Association's 2026 New York Benefit Dinner.
Its wines were served on 5 November 2026 to hundreds of business, government and diplomacy leaders at the Manhattan gala.
Each guest took home a bottle of the 2019 Samantha's Paddock Mélange Traditionnel, the estate's flagship Cabernet blend.

MARKET.head: Wine stays Australia's top-bought alcohol as drinking declines and spending per visit rises
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report: 55% of Australians buy wine, ahead of spirits at 46% and beer at 44%.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% drink more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from around 23% a year ago.

MARKET.head: Marnong Estate releases first Reserve Chardonnay alongside new cool-climate range
MARKET.summ: Marnong Estate has unveiled its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay as a part its new collection of cool-climate expressions from the estate's Sunbury vineyards. The 2024 Reserve Chardonnay leads the new range which features the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay and 2025 Estate Chardonnay, offering “distinct interpretations of the...
takeaways: Marnong Estate, a Sunbury winery, has released its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay, the 2024 vintage, as part of a new spring collection.
The collection also includes the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay, the 2025 Estate Chardonnay and the 2026 Estate Sangiovese Rosé, its first rosé from that fruit.
The new releases are sold nationally through independent merchants, at the cellar door and online via the winery's website.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek Chinese importers at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Wine imports from Moldova to China reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026, per Chinese customs data.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of its wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine small formats gain traction amid moderation and single-person households
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22% to about 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Australian 187mL export volumes grew 39%, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Single-person households make up 26% of Australian households, up from 18% in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules now restrict vague eco claims on wine labels and marketing
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: Directive (EU) 2024/825, called EmpCo, began enforcement on September 27 and bans vague environmental claims on consumer products.
Terms like "eco-friendly" and "green" must be specified and substantiated, and unverified sustainability badges are prohibited.
Enforcement is left to individual EU member states, with fines of up to four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded value as Burgundy's share jumps to 20.8%
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages the top-traded by value.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading producers.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6%, led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: India-EU trade deal cuts wine tariffs, but state rules still complicate entry
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: India's 150% tariff on EU wine will fall to 20% for premium and 30% for medium wines, phased in over time.
Alcohol is regulated state by state in India, so market entry means separate routes in each state, not one national market.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine in 2025, worth US$28.8 million, with volume up 13.7% year on year.

MARKET.head: German wine imports into China rise in volume, value and average price
MARKET.summ: Imports rose in volume, value and average price in the first nine months, offering an encouraging backdrop for 45 wineries and importers heading to the German Pavilion
takeaways: China imported 4.23 million liters of bottled German wine in the first nine months of 2026, up 8%.
Import value rose 11% to US$22.49 million, while the average import price increased 3%.
Germany brings 45 wineries and importers to ProWine Shanghai, Nov. 10–12, including over 10 first-time Chinese exhibitors.

MARKET.head: California table grape supply to last through December for holiday promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: California Table Grape Commission says grapes stay available in promotable volumes throughout December after harvest ends mid-November.
Commission President Ian LeMay says steady shipments and cold storage let supply continue well into December despite an early harvest start.
Commission consumer research finds 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes, versus fewer than 5% preferring imports.

CULTURE.head: Seventeen sommeliers name the bottles they always order from menus
CULTURE.summ: Exploration is one of wine’s greatest virtues. A bottle shop or wine menu can take you from the Rheinessen’s steep hills to the peaks of Mendoza to the sea salt-dusted cliffs of the San Luis Obispo Coast. Even within a single region, drinkers can taste a world of grapes, terroirs, and climates.
takeaways: Seventeen sommeliers were asked to name the wines they always order when they see them on a menu.
Picks include Lady of the Sunshine Chene Vineyard Pinot Noir, Antinori Tignanello, and Lodi's 135-year-old Bechtold Vineyard Cinsault.
Other choices include Les Jardins de la Martinière Shi Ro 2018, Jonata La Sangre Syrah, and Valentini Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo.

CULTURE.head: Four South Australian wine professionals win overseas knowledge exchange bursaries for 2026-27
CULTURE.summ: Four South Australian wine industry representatives have been selected to travel to some of the world’s most renowned wine regions to “connect with international experts and explore new ideas and innovations”. The South Australian Government explained that ‘The Great Wine Capitals Outbound Knowledge Exchange Bursary Program’...
takeaways: Four South Australian wine industry professionals were selected for the 2026-27 Great Wine Capitals Outbound Knowledge Exchange Bursary Program.
Recipients Jodie Armstrong, Nicole Brasier, Susi Whiting and Luke Willis each receive a $6,000 bursary for travel between October 2026 and March 2027.
The bursaries fund visits to Great Wine Capitals Global Network regions to exchange knowledge on sustainability, climate adaptation and consumer engagement.

CULTURE.head: Beaujolais Nouveau's midnight release became wine's original viral marketing event
CULTURE.summ: Decades before brands built anticipation for limited-edition drops with countdowns, celebrity appearances, or social media buzz, wine had its own version of the hype cycle. The days may be shorter and the air crisper, but in the world of wine, November is when things start heating up. This is especially true for those who have...
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau, made from Gamay, is released at 12:01 a.m. on the third Thursday of November, a date set by France's INAO in 1985.
Georges Duboeuf, founder of his négociant house in 1964, helped turn the release into an international phenomenon through publicity stunts.
The wine is low in tannin and alcohol, meant to be drunk soon after release, and is marketed as a Thanksgiving pairing.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts how she came to work in the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this episode of VinePair's Wine 101 podcast, an informal conversation with Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wine Cellars.
Smith Story describes her personal journey into the wine industry and how she came to work in it.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI updates agrochemical lookup app on Apple and Android stores
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google stores.
The free app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the Dog book.
Users who already have the app are asked to update it to keep receiving future updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting five of the best from Torres, Penedès, Spain
NEWSLETTERS.summ: At the recent Star Wine List Inspiration Day I tasted through these fine wines from leading Catalunyan producer Torres. They
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Torres Milmanda Chardonnay 2022 from Conca de Barberà was the first Torres vintage made without malolactic fermentation, with reduced ageing time.
Torres Mas de la Rosa Vinyes Velles Porrera 2020, a single old-vineyard Priorat, scored 96/100, the top score among the five wines tasted.
Torres Mas La Plana 2020, a Penedès Cabernet Sauvignon first made in 1970, was also rated 96/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/8/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Young winemakers in Burgundy are tending vines and shaping the region's future, per The Burgundy Outlook.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relative newcomer to Bourgueil whose domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot produces one blended entry-level cuvée and single-vineyard wines from his best slope parcels, with two cuvées parcellaires set to join from 2020.
Revillot, from a Mâconnais farming family, trained in Dijon and worked at Domaine Drouhin in Oregon and Newton Johnson in South Africa before arriving in the Loire in 2010.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava takes its name from the cellars dug to store the wine, becoming a formal Spanish legal label term in 1972.
The Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022 from Penedès is made from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada and aged 40 months.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow visited Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop set for November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo, Ayuso and Campos Reales Verdejo, and Piqueras El Abuelo were highlighted, with many wines priced RMB12 to RMB24 per bottle.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Columnist is judging at the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, the only competition known with a dedicated orange and amber wine panel.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber received mid-90s scores from all six judges, earning an instant grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a biodynamic right-bank Bordeaux estate, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Traditional labels? Suck My Duck
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Never say that wine labelling regulations are a subject devoid of humour. The Tribunal Correctionnel de Paris recently heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over his provocative packaging. Vellas’s edgy cuvées have included “Little Fuck,” “Bad Angel” (its label...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A Paris court heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over provocative labels like "Suck My Duck".
Bordeaux has lost a fifth of its vineyard area in four years, with 30,000 ha set to be uprooted by end of December.
Bordeaux labels remain largely old-fashioned, featuring château pictures or family crests, while natural producers in less prestigious regions use eye-catching labels.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks dropping back on Sunday mark the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
Meg Maker shares a list of kitchen tools she uses year-round that become even more essential during festive cooking.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near Pontevedra, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the O Grove estuary.
The underwater-aged Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months at 13-16C and is compared against the 2025 'Standard' bottling, of which about 120,000 bottles are made annually.
The author's experience is that underwater-aged wines tend to taste more advanced in age and less fresh than landbound counterparts, which he views as largely a gimmick.
